rubric.title: Evidence rubric
rubric.stamp: Evidence rubric {version} · published {date} · changes are curator-only and announced
rubric.blurb: The adjudicator grades each evidence item by tier, then adjusts it for relevance, recency and independence. The suggestion's score is set by its strongest item. A curator decides what the rubric cannot.

example.A: A saved lab run in the IDE that reproduces the claimed change. A derive script diff. A runnable notebook with data.
example.B: Peer-reviewed paper. Preprint with code. Standard or regulation text. Official specification. Audited filing.
example.C: Official documentation, pricing page, changelog, release note or model card from the vendor concerned.
example.D: Independent benchmark (Artificial Analysis, Epoch, RouterArena-class). Systematic review. Regulator guidance.
example.E: Named engineer's technical post with method and numbers. Conference talk with slides. Open-source repository with measurements.
example.F: News article. Secondary summary. Textbook without primary citation.
example.G: Social media post. Forum comment. Unsourced blog. Personal assertion.
example.U: Link cannot be opened. Document not supplied. Claim without artefact. Graded as unverifiable, not as weak.

rule.statement: The strongest item decides. Ten weak items never equal one strong one.
rule.formula: score = max( base × relevance × recency × independence )
rule.formulaBonus: + {bonus} once, if a second independent item is tier {tier} or above
rule.note: Never a sum. Never an average. Corroboration adds {bonus} at most.

note.ILLUSTRATIVE: an assumption, not evidence; replaced only by A

adjustments.label: Adjustment factors

relevance.name: Relevance
relevance.rule: Evidence addresses the anchored claim directly / partially / tangentially. Graded with the source opened.

recency.name: Recency
recency.rule: Fast-moving figures only: prices, deadlines, model versions, benchmarks. {windows} / older. Stable facts are unadjusted.

independence.name: Independence
independence.rule: No stake / the vendor concerned / the contributor's own employer.

corroboration.name: Corroboration
corroboration.rule: A second independent item at tier {tier} or above. Added once, after the strongest item is chosen.

adjustments.footer: the adjudicator does not see contributor identity beyond verified / unverified
